author: fwyzard
body: #### PR description: This PR partially addresses #52253. Currently every module call copies the job's `ServiceToken` (a `std::shared_ptr`), or locks a `ServiceWeakToken` to it, and release it again: in `Path::runNextWorkerAsync` / `workerFinished`, in the worker tasks, in every `ServiceRegistry::Operate`. All threads of the job therefore update the same atomic reference count, whose cache line bounces between cores and sockets; on large two-socket machines this is a bottleneck for the whole job. This PR makes `ServiceToken` a non-owning handle to the services: a plain pointer, trivially copyable, with no reference counting. The ownership moves to a new `OwningServiceToken`, returned by `ServiceRegistry::createSet`, `createContaining` and `createServicesFromConfig`, and held by the owners of the services: `EventProcessor`, `TestProcessor`, `TestSourceProcessor`, `PythonEventProcessor`, `cmsRun`, `PileUp`, and the standalone tools and tests that create their own service set. `ServiceRegistry::Operate` and `presentToken()` are non-owning; the new `ServiceRegistry::LockedOperate` holds an `OwningServiceToken` and makes its services available. All the asynchronous tasks and callbacks (event paths, workers, transforms, stream and global transitions, EventSetup callbacks, delayed reader) capture the caller's `ServiceToken` instead of a `ServiceWeakToken`. `ServiceWeakToken` is renamed `WeakServiceToken`, and remains for objects that can outlive the services, e.g. the `TFile` of `TStorageFactoryFile`. The `OwningServiceToken` is passed down the construction of a service set: the `EventProcessor`, `TestProcessor` and `TestSourceProcessor` constructors take one, `ScheduleItems::initServices` and `addTNS` update it in place, and `ServiceRegistry::createSet` / `createContaining` take the base service set as an `OwningServiceToken`, whose `ServicesManager` the new one keeps alive. A `ServicesManager` can only be created by `ServicesManager::create()`, which builds it in a `std::shared_ptr` and only then creates its services, so that a service can take an owning or a weak token to its own service set in its constructor. `ServicesManager` derives from `std::enable_shared_from_this` only so that an owning or weak token can be obtained from a non-owning one, as `PileUp` and `TStorageFactoryFile` do. The `SourceCoordinator`, created before the services, holds a non-owning `ServiceToken` set once they exist. Behaviour changes for code outside the framework: - a `ServiceToken` must not outlive the `OwningServiceToken` that owns the services; it cannot be obtained from a temporary `OwningServiceToken` (compile-time error); - code that creates its own services must keep the result in an `OwningServiceToken` (`edm::ServiceToken token = edm::ServiceRegistry::createSet(...)` does not compile any more); this affects the standalone tools and the unit tests of `CondCore`, `FWStorage`, `HeterogeneousCore`, `PhysicsTools` and `FWCore`, updated here; - the `EventProcessor`, `TestProcessor` and `TestSourceProcessor` constructors, and `createSet` / `createContaining` with a base service set, take an `OwningServiceToken` instead of a `ServiceToken`; - `ServiceWeakToken` is renamed `WeakServiceToken`, and its `lock()` returns an `OwningServiceToken`; - `setupSiteLocalConfig()` returns a `ServiceRegistry::LockedOperate` that owns the service it makes available; - `connect` and `copySlotsTo` are only available on `OwningServiceToken`; `connectTo` and `copySlotsFrom` are removed from the tokens (they were unused); - a `ServicesManager` can only be created with `ServicesManager::create()`, which returns a `std::shared_ptr`; only the `ServiceRegistry` and its unit tests did this; - the module-facing `doTransformAsync` / `transformAsync_` take a `ServiceToken const&` instead of a `ServiceWeakToken const&`; no module outside `FWCore/Framework` implements them. This replaces the earlier version of this PR, which kept the owning token and added a separate `ServiceRegistry::OperateNonOwning` with tokens passed by reference to the tasks, following the [suggestion](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/52158#issuecomment-6200819862) by @Dr15Jones. Making the non-owning handle the default removes the second `Operate`, the reference-lifetime conventions in the tasks, and the changes to `ESProductResolverTemplate`, for the same performance. ##### Measurements HLT menu `/online/collisions/2026/2e34/v1.3/HLT/V2`, run 402360 HLTPhysics data read with `DAQSource` from local FRD files, CPU only, jobs pinned with `taskset` to N cores and both of their SMT siblings (threads = streams = cpus), 2 concurrent lumisections, 4 repetitions per point, average standard deviation. Throughput from the `ThroughputService` over at least 60 s per job. Scaling with the number of cores on a 2 AMD EPYC 9655 machine (2 96 Zen 5 cores; the container leaves out one core per socket, so a full socket has 95 cores and the full machine 190), cores added in order, `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-23-1100` with and without this PR. The dashed line is the IB extrapolated linearly from one full CCD (8 cores), so the L3 sharing within a CCD is not counted as a loss. The left plot shows the throughput as measured, the right one the throughput normalised to 3.0 GHz, the clock frequency observed when the full machine is in use: The IB stops scaling at about 64-95 cores (446.3 2.3 ev/s with 190 cores, at 3.77 GHz); with this PR the throughput keeps growing to the full machine (772.4 0.2 ev/s at 2.97 GHz, +73%). At a fixed clock it follows the extrapolation from one CCD, within 1.5%, up to about 80 cores, and reaches 90% of it on the full machine. One job on all the cores of the machine, compared with concurrent jobs each pinned to one socket or to one CCD (`CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-23-1100`, average standard deviation of 4 repetitions, ev/s): | 2 EPYC 9655 | IB | this PR | | |---|---|---|---| | one job, 190 cores | 447.2 3.9 | 771.7 2.7 | +72.6% 1.6% | | two jobs, one per socket (95 cores each) | 761.5 0.6 | 845.6 1.2 | +11.0% 0.2% | | 24 jobs, one per CCD (8 cores each) | 869.5 0.3 | 871.6 0.2 | +0.2% 0.1% | With the previous version of this PR (`CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-19-1100`, 3 repetitions), on two other machines: | machine | one job, all cores: IB | previous version | | two jobs, one per socket: IB | previous version | | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2 EPYC 9534 (124 cores) | 311.2 2.4 | 391.4 4.9 | +25.8% 1.8% | 435.4 0.4 | 436.7 2.6 | +0.3% 0.6% | | 2 EPYC 9965 (382 cores) | 410 1 | 502 16 | +22.4% 3.9% | 852.7 0.5 | 1306.2 1.9 | +53.2% 0.2% | On the 9965 this PR improves all results, but the single full-machine job remains far below the two per-socket jobs. This will be addressed separately. #### PR validation: As of 80d202dbb31ffaa2dfd51f1ac1574528b1ac502c all unit tests pass, and the matrix workflows run without issues. The final version of the PR was tested in 267 benchmark jobs on the 2 EPYC 9655 (the socket configurations, the scan over the number of cores and the perf checks above); all of them completed successfully. A previous version of this PR was also tested on two other machines (2 EPYC 9534, 2 EPYC 9965): the HLT gave identical decisions on 4000 events (16 threads, no prescales), and all benchmarks ran without encountering any issues.
title: Rework the Services ownership to improve scaling to large number of cores
